turns.user: I want to print a 600 mm high, 1.5 m long wall with two filaments across the thickness, 25 mm nozzle, 50 mm/s, open time 60 min. The material has a static yield stress of 3 kPa and Athix of 1 Pa/s. Is it printable, and what is the layer cycle-time window?
turns.text:
I’ll check the available pmpredict buildability and print-job tools, then evaluate the wall using the stated dimensions, extrusion setup, open time, and rheology.
**No, not under the assessed setup.** The physical verdict is **non_printable**: the model predicts free-wall buckling at layer 17 and plastic collapse around layer 34, before the 48 layers needed for 600 mm. It estimates a maximum height of 212.5 mm after accounting for buckling.

The cycle-time window is **not feasible**: about **161 seconds minimum** for stability, but **75 seconds maximum** to finish within the 60-minute open time. Your specified 50 mm/s gives a 60-second cycle for the 3 m layer path, below the stability minimum. The assessment estimates that, at this cycle, the material would need roughly **7.8 kPa static yield stress** and **2.68 Pa/s Athix**.

I used the tool’s default layer height of 12.5 mm (half the nozzle diameter) and layer width of 29.61 mm (1.2 times nozzle diameter); it assumes no dwell. The empirical collapse probability is secondary to the physical verdict. These calculations are screening guidance, so verify any revised setup experimentally.
